patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Airtable and Wrike share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Comparison thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Airtable only if your buying job matches “Flexible database / app platform with interfaces and light project apps — Team from ~$20/u” rather than Wrike's shape. Choose Wrike only if your buying job matches “Enterprise/agency work management with proofing, intake and resourcing — Team from $10/use” rather than Airtable's shape. Workflow advantage: Airtable leans shared coverage; Wrike leans resource-planning, team-collaboration-work. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Airtable and Wrike share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Airtable is Flexible database / app platform with interfaces and light project apps — Team from ~$20/user/mo annual.; Wrike is Enterprise/agency work management with proofing, intake and resourcing — Team from $10/user/mo annual..
- Workflow coverage skew: Airtable-leaning — vs Wrike-leaning resource-planning, team-collaboration-work.
- Researched limits: Airtable — Higher seat floors than Notion/ClickUp; Wrike — Business tier pricing jump.

Limitations — Airtable: Higher seat floors than Notion/ClickUp; Builder complexity; Wrike: Business tier pricing jump; Heavier admin than lightweight tools.

Poor-fit cases: Airtable is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Higher seat floors than Notion/ClickUp · Wrike is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Business tier pricing jump · Avoid Airtable if you actually need Wrike's motion (Enterprise/agency work management with proofing, intake and resourcing — Team fr)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
